verses.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ δι’ ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἐν οἴκῳ ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: Kai eiselthōn palin eis Kapharnaoum di’ hēmerōn ēkousthē hoti en oikō estin
verses.literal: A few days later Jesus went back to . . . . . . Capernaum And when the people heard that He was home
verses.literalPt: Alguns dias depois, voltou Jesus a Cafarnaum, e soube-se que ele estava em casa.

verses.original: καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον
verses.transliteration: kai synēchthēsan polloi hōste mēketi chōrein mēde ta pros tēn thyran kai elalei autois ton logon
verses.literal: they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room not even outside the door as Jesus spoke the word to them
verses.literalPt: Muitos afluíram ali, a ponto de já não haver lugar nem junto à porta; e ele lhes dirigia a palavra.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων
verses.transliteration: Kai erchontai pherontes pros auton paralytikon airomenon hypo tessarōn
verses.literal: Then a paralytic was brought to Him carried by four men
verses.literalPt: Trouxeram-lhe um paralítico, carregado por quatro homens;

verses.original: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο
verses.transliteration: kai mē dynamenoi prosenenkai autō dia ton ochlon apestegasan tēn stegēn hopou ēn kai exoryxantes chalōsi ton krabatton hopou ho paralytikos katekeito
verses.literal: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd they uncovered the roof above Him . . . made an opening and lowered the paralytic on his mat
verses.literalPt: e, não podendo apresentar-lho por causa da multidão, desladrilharam o eirado por cima de Jesus e, feita uma abertura, arrearam o leito em que jazia o paralítico.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ Τέκνον ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι
verses.transliteration: Kai idōn ho Iēsous tēn pistin autōn legei tō paralytikō Teknon aphientai sou hai hamartiai
verses.literal: When Jesus saw their faith He said to the paralytic Son your sins are forgiven
verses.literalPt: Vendo Jesus a fé que eles tinham, disse ao paralítico: Filho, perdoados são os teus pecados.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Ēsan de tines tōn grammateōn ekei kathēmenoi kai dialogizomenoi en tais kardiais autōn
verses.literal: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts
verses.literalPt: Estavam, porém, ali sentados alguns escribas, que discorriam nos seus corações:

verses.original: Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ βλασφημεῖ τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός
verses.transliteration: Ti houtos houtōs lalei blasphēmei tis dynatai aphienai hamartias ei mē heis ho Theos
verses.literal: Why does this man speak like this He is blaspheming Who can forgive sins but . . . God alone
verses.literalPt: Por que fala assim este homem? Ele blasfema; quem pode perdoar pecados senão só um, que é Deus?

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys epignous ho Iēsous tō pneumati autou hoti houtōs dialogizontai en heautois legei autois Ti tauta dialogizesthe en tais kardiais hymōn
verses.literal: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves Why are you thinking these things in your hearts He asked . . .
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus, percebendo logo em seu espírito que eles assim discorriam dentro de si, perguntou-lhes: Por que discorreis sobre essas coisas em vossos corações?

verses.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει
verses.transliteration: ti estin eukopōteron eipein tō paralytikō Aphientai sou hai hamartiai ē eipein Egeire kai aron ton krabatton sou kai peripatei
verses.literal: Which is easier to say to a paralytic Your sins are forgiven or to say Get up pick up your mat and walk
verses.literalPt: Qual é mais fácil? Dizer ao paralítico: Perdoados são os teus pecados, ou dizer: Levanta-te, toma o teu leito e anda?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ
verses.transliteration: hina de eidēte hoti exousian echei ho Huios tou anthrōpou aphienai hamartias epi tēs gēs legei tō paralytikō
verses.literal: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins He said to the paralytic
verses.literalPt: Para que saibais que o Filho do Homem tem sobre a terra autoridade para perdoar pecados — disse ao paralítico:

verses.original: Σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου
verses.transliteration: Soi legō egeire aron ton krabatton sou kai hypage eis ton oikon sou
verses.literal: I tell you get up pick up your mat and go home
verses.literalPt: A ti te digo: Levanta-te, toma o teu leito e vai para tua casa.

verses.original: Καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ἐναντίον πάντων ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι Οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδομεν
verses.transliteration: Kai ēgerthē kai euthys aras ton krabatton exēlthen enantion pantōn hōste existasthai pantas kai doxazein ton Theon legontas hoti Houtōs oudepote eidomen
verses.literal: And immediately the man got up picked up his mat and walked out in front of them all As a result they were all astounded and glorified God saying We have never seen anything like this
verses.literalPt: Ele se levantou e, no mesmo instante, tomando o seu leito, retirou-se à vista de todos de modo que todos ficaram atônitos e glorificaram a Deus, dizendo: Nunca vimos coisa semelhante.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: Kai exēlthen palin para tēn thalassan kai pas ho ochlos ērcheto pros auton kai edidasken autous
verses.literal: Once again Jesus went out beside the sea All the people came to Him and He taught them there
verses.literalPt: Saiu, outra vez, para a beira-mar; toda a multidão vinha ter com ele, e ele os ensinava.

verses.original: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai paragōn eiden Leuin ton tou Halphaiou kathēmenon epi to telōnion kai legei autō Akolouthei moi kai anastas ēkolouthēsen autō
verses.literal: As He was walking along He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth Follow Me He told him and Levi got up and followed Him
verses.literalPt: Quando ia passando, viu a Levi, filho de Alfeu, sentado na coletoria, e disse-lhe: Segue-me. Ele se levantou e o seguiu.

verses.original: Καὶ γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai ginetai katakeisthai auton en tē oikia autou kai polloi telōnai kai hamartōloi synanekeinto tō Iēsou kai tois mathētais autou ēsan gar polloi kai ēkolouthoun autō
verses.literal: While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples for there were many who followed Him
verses.literalPt: Estando Jesus à mesa na casa de Levi, sentaram-se também com ele e com seus discípulos muitos publicanos e pecadores; pois havia muitos que o seguiam.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων ἰδόντες ὅτι ἐσθίει μετὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει
verses.transliteration: kai hoi grammateis tōn Pharisaiōn idontes hoti esthiei meta tōn hamartōlōn kai telōnōn elegon tois mathētais autou Hoti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiei
verses.literal: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people they asked . . . His disciples Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners
verses.literalPt: Vendo os escribas dos fariseus que ele comia com os pecadores e publicanos, perguntaram aos discípulos dele: Como é que ele come com os publicanos e pecadores?

verses.original: Καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλ’ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς
verses.transliteration: Kai akousas ho Iēsous legei autois hoti Ou chreian echousin hoi ischyontes iatrou all’ hoi kakōs echontes ouk ēlthon kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous
verses.literal: On hearing this Jesus told them It is not the healthy who need a doctor but the sick . . . I have not come to call the righteous but sinners
verses.literalPt: Jesus, ouvindo isso, respondeu-lhes: Os sãos não precisam de médico, mas sim os enfermos; eu não vim chamar os justos, mas os pecadores.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai ēsan hoi mathētai Iōannou kai hoi Pharisaioi nēsteuontes kai erchontai kai legousin autō Dia ti hoi mathētai Iōannou kai hoi mathētai tōn Pharisaiōn nēsteuousin hoi de soi mathētai ou nēsteuousin
verses.literal: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting So people came to Jesus and asked Why . . . don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees
verses.literalPt: ( Ora, os discípulos de João e os fariseus estavam jejuando.) Eles vieram perguntar-lhe: Por que jejuam os discípulos de João e os dos fariseus, mas os teus não jejuam?

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετ’ αὐτῶν οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autois ho Iēsous Mē dynantai hoi huioi tou nymphōnos en hō ho nymphios met’ autōn estin nēsteuein hoson chronon echousin ton nymphion met’ autōn ou dynantai nēsteuein
verses.literal: Jesus replied How can the guests of the bridegroom fast . . . while He is with them As long as . . . He is with them they cannot fast
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhes Jesus: Podem, porventura, jejuar os convidados para o casamento, enquanto o noivo está com eles? Durante o tempo que têm consigo o noivo, não podem jejuar.

verses.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ
verses.transliteration: eleusontai de hēmerai hotan aparthē ap’ autōn ho nymphios kai tote nēsteusousin en ekeinē tē hēmera
verses.literal: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them then . . . . . . . . . . . . they will fast
verses.literalPt: Dias, porém, virão, em que lhes será tirado o noivo; nesses dias, jejuarão.

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν εἰ δὲ μή αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται
verses.transliteration: Oudeis epiblēma rhakous agnaphou epiraptei epi himation palaion ei de mē airei to plērōma ap’ autou to kainon tou palaiou kai cheiron schisma ginetai
verses.literal: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment If he does . . . . . . the new piece will pull away - from the old - and a worse tear will result
verses.literalPt: Ninguém cose remendo de pano novo em vestido velho; de outra forma, o remendo novo tira parte do velho, e torna-se maior a rotura.

verses.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος τοὺς ἀσκούς καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς
verses.transliteration: Kai oudeis ballei oinon neon eis askous palaious ei de mē rhēxei ho oinos tous askous kai ho oinos apollytai kai hoi askoi alla oinon neon eis askous kainous
verses.literal: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins If he does . . . . . . the wine will burst the skins and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined Instead new wine is poured into new wineskins
verses.literalPt: Ninguém põe vinho novo em odres velhos; de outra forma, o vinho fará arrebentar os odres, e perder-se-á o vinho, e também os odres. Pelo contrário, vinho novo é posto em odres novos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι διὰ τῶν σπορίμων καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας
verses.transliteration: Kai egeneto auton en tois sabbasin paraporeuesthai dia tōn sporimōn kai hoi mathētai autou ērxanto hodon poiein tillontes tous stachyas
verses.literal: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along . . .
verses.literalPt: Caminhando Jesus pelas searas em um sábado, os seus discípulos, ao passarem, começaram a colher espigas.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἴδε τί ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν
verses.transliteration: kai hoi Pharisaioi elegon autō Ide ti poiousin tois sabbasin ho ouk exestin
verses.literal: So the Pharisees said to Him Look why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath
verses.literalPt: Os fariseus lhe perguntaram: Olha, por que fazem eles no sábado o que não é lícito?

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai legei autois Oudepote anegnōte ti epoiēsen Dauid hote chreian eschen kai epeinasen autos kai hoi met’ autou
verses.literal: Jesus replied . . . Have you never read what David did when he and his companions . . . . . . were hungry and in need
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes respondeu: Nunca lestes o que fez Davi, quando se viu em necessidade e teve fome, ele e seus companheiros?

verses.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἱερεῖς καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν
verses.transliteration: pōs eisēlthen eis ton oikon tou Theou epi Abiathar archiereōs kai tous artous tēs protheseōs ephagen hous ouk exestin phagein ei mē tous hiereis kai edōken kai tois syn autō ousin
verses.literal: During the high priesthood of Abiathar he entered . . . the house of God and ate the consecrated bread . . . . . . which was lawful only . . . for the priests And he gave some to his companions . . . . . . . . . as well
verses.literalPt: Como entrou na Casa de Deus, sendo Abiatar sumo sacerdote, e comeu os pães da proposição, os quais só aos sacerdotes era lícito comer, e ainda deu aos seus companheiros?

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois To sabbaton dia ton anthrōpon egeneto kai ouch ho anthrōpos dia to sabbaton
verses.literal: Then Jesus declared The Sabbath was made for man not man for the Sabbath
verses.literalPt: Acrescentou: O sábado foi feito por causa do homem e não o homem por causa do sábado;

verses.original: ὥστε κύριός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ σαββάτου
verses.transliteration: hōste kyrios estin ho Huios tou anthrōpou kai tou sabbatou
verses.literal: Therefore the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath
verses.literalPt: assim, o Filho do Homem é senhor até do sábado.
